english: Let $f:(-\infty,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ and $g:\left(-\dfrac{5}{2},\infty\right)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\sqrt{4-2^{x+1}}$ and $g(x)=\log_e(2x+5)$. Let $h(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}+\dfrac{g(x)}{f(x)}$. The set of all real numbers $x$ for which $h(x)$ is defined is of the form $(a,b)\setminus\{c\}$, where $a<c<b$. Then the value of $a+b+c$ is ______.

solution_full: $f(x)=\sqrt{4-2^{x+1}}$ is real when $4-2^{x+1}\geq0$, i.e. $2^{x+1}\leq2^{2}$. As $2^{t}$ is increasing, this means $x+1\leq2$, i.e. $x\leq1$.
Both terms of $h$ need $f$ and $g$ to be defined, so $x\in\left(-\dfrac52,1\right]$.
The term $\dfrac{f}{g}$ needs $g(x)\neq0$. Now $\log_e(2x+5)=0\iff2x+5=1\iff x=-2$, and $-2\in\left(-\dfrac52,1\right]$, so $x=-2$ is removed.
The term $\dfrac{g}{f}$ needs $f(x)\neq0$. Now $\sqrt{4-2^{x+1}}=0\iff2^{x+1}=4\iff x=1$, so the right end point $1$ is removed.
Hence $h$ is defined exactly on $\left(-\dfrac52,1\right)\setminus\{-2\}$, which gives $a=-\dfrac52$, $b=1$, $c=-2$ (and indeed $a<c<b$).
originality_note: New: f/g + g/f forces the zeros of both functions out of the common domain; one zero is the end point of the radical's domain, which turns a closed end into an open one (way 5). Closest known: domain of a single quotient of a radical and a logarithm. Different because: the two reciprocal terms remove a point from each function, and the student must notice that the zero of f is the boundary point.

concept_use.Algebra of functions (f+g, fg, f/g) and: h = f/g + g/f is defined on the common domain minus the zeros of g (x = -2) and of f (x = 1).
concept_use.Domain of algebraic, logarithmic, expone: The exponential-radical condition 2^(x+1) <= 4 gives x <= 1 and the logarithm condition 2x + 5 > 0 gives x > -5/2.
